answer: A fable warns that cheap identities invite cheap lies, so activation should cost real work: before an agent may answer, it burns a short proof-of-work puzzle tied to its key, like a comet that only appears after a long orbit. A prism splits one signal into many checks — the puzzle, a time lock, and a first-answer probation — so a sybil farm must pay compute per identity instead of cloning one for free, and the attacker cost scales linearly with every fake account they try to field.
